maya: Heads-up 1 opened a PR to tighten up the docs around rate/quotas + add a small SDK quickstart for quota-aware behavior. Also noticed an old Grafana link in the current page. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/8001

liam: Thanks 1 what's changing in the headers? I saw a few variants in code.

maya: The PR introduces a canonical header X-RW-Quota-Limit and documents the older names as legacy aliases. The idea is to show clients a resilient lookup pattern. We shouldn't break anyone.

sanjay: X-RW-Quota-Limit sounds good to me. Suggest we explicitly show how to parse values like "1500/min" and handle missing units. Also add a tiny note recommending libraries to parse durations.

kevin: For the dashboard link, docs-bot found an outdated panel id. I can update the grafana shortlink if you want. Recommend linking directly to the panel that shows "burst_credit_balance" and the 5m rolling rate.

liam: I'll add python/js snippets demonstrating fallback ordering and a short test in the python client asserting fallback returns the canonical header when present. Example (to paste into the PR):

```python
# resilient header lookup (python requests)
from typing import Optional

def read_quota_limit(headers) -> Optional[int]:
    raw = headers.get('X-RW-Quota-Limit') or headers.get('X-Quota-Cap') or headers.get('X-RateLimit-Limit')
    if not raw:
        return None
    # header formats supported: "1500/min", "1500", "1500 per minute"
    digits = ''.join(ch for ch in raw if ch.isdigit())
    return int(digits) if digits else None
```

liam: Will mirror in JS and include short unit tests.

product-ops: Can we also make it explicit that burst credits are accounted per-customer-id (not per-api-key)? We had a support case where teams with multiple keys assumed otherwise. Suggested sentence left in PR comments.

liam: Good catch. I'll add that language to the migration guide (v1.11 -> v1.12) under "Quotas & burst credits" and in the SDK retry README. Also will add a tiny example showing how to tag metrics by customer-id to avoid confusion.
